findings.summary: "The property becomes observable only when a PRODUCTION resend exists" is falsified by measurement: a production resend exists today in RemoteSequencer.commitAll, it is unpinned, and a behaviour-level pin for it reds under the defect and greens clean -- I built and measured both.
findings.detail: The cell's proof is sound for the M5.2 HOIST and I re-verified it (see the verified claims below). It is NOT sound for the row's headline property, "a retry reuses its triple", which the final sentence generalises to. RemoteSequencer.commitAll:102-103 IS a production retry: on NotTheLeaseholderException it re-reads the lease and, if it moved, resends requests.get(0) -- the same request object -- to the new holder. That resend reuses its triple in production and NOTHING constrains it to. MEASURED, out of tree, on a worktree at d48547a: replacing `requests.get(0)` at the follow arm with `new CommitRequest(r.podId(), r.incarnationId(), r.flushSeq() + 1, r.segmentKey(), r.recordCounts())` -- the exact defect Sequencer's own javadoc names ("a caller that mints a fresh flushSeq for the retry is submitting a different commit") -- leaves :sequencer:test at 495 tests, 0 failures, gradle exit 0. The delta lands with a flushSeq the pod never issued and no assertion sees it. THE PIN THE ROW SAYS CANNOT EXIST: I wrote `aFollowedResendCarriesTheSAMETripleAsTheRefusedAttempt` in RemoteSequencerTest (51 lines, the fixture of aLeaseThatMovesDURINGTheCommitIsFollowedAfterOneRefusal:124 with a transport that appends each request to a list): assertThat(sent).hasSize(2) then assertThat(sent.get(1)).isEqualTo(sent.get(0)). MEASURED: RED under the mutation (the only failure in 12 RemoteSequencerTest cases), GREEN on the clean tree at 496 tests, 0 failures. It is a behaviour assertion, not an implementation-shape one -- it uses record equality, not identity, so a refactor that rebuilds an equal request still passes, and it constrains what the peer receives rather than how commitAll is written. It does NOT red under the M5.2 revert, and it is not claimed to: it pins the property at the seam where a retry actually exists. CONSEQUENCE OF LEAVING THE CELL AS WRITTEN: it records a buildable pin as impossible-in-principle, so the next reader does not try, and the one production retry in the tree can start minting fresh triples with 495/495 green. That is the "converts an unknown into false confidence" failure, one level up from a weak test. FIX, either way and both cheap: narrow the sentence to what was actually proved -- the hoist is unobservable, and criterion 4's missing piece is an AMBIGUOUS-reply resend on the DefaultIngest path (SPEC.md:320 says exactly that, and anAMBIGUOUSFailureIsNOTResent:294 shows RemoteSequencer deliberately does not resend that case) -- and open a row for the refusal-following resend pin; or land the test with this commit. What must not stand is the unqualified "only when a PRODUCTION resend exists".
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED on a worktree at d48547a, out of tree. Defect: at RemoteSequencer.commitAll:102-103 the follow-the-lease resend sends `new CommitRequest(r.podId(), r.incarnationId(), r.flushSeq()+1, r.segmentKey(), r.recordCounts())` instead of `requests.get(0)` -- a retry that mints a fresh triple, the exact thing 'a retry reuses its triple' forbids and Sequencer's javadoc names as committing the same records twice. Result: :sequencer:test 495 tests, 0 failures, gradle exit 0 -- nothing in the tree notices, and the chain records a flushSeq the pod never issued. Construction that catches it: `aFollowedResendCarriesTheSAMETripleAsTheRefusedAttempt` in RemoteSequencerTest -- the fixture of aLeaseThatMovesDURINGTheCommitIsFollowedAfterOneRefusal:124 with a SequencerTransport that appends every request it is handed to a list, then assertThat(sent).hasSize(2) and assertThat(sent.get(1)).isEqualTo(sent.get(0)). MEASURED RED under the mutation (sole failure of the 12 cases in that class) and GREEN on the clean tree (496 tests, 0 failures). Record equality, not identity, so a resend rebuilt from equal fields still passes -- it breaks only when the resend is a different commit.
